decisions.rationale: The author directly assures future delivery by their team.
evidence: Our conservation team will send you the matching condition cards tomorrow

decisions.rationale: The author recalls an old promise without renewing it.
evidence: Last winter I promised to send the tape inventory by the end of that week. I am recounting the old arrangement here.

decisions.rationale: The author unconditionally commits to sending concrete packets.
evidence: I will send you the accession packets for the dune-grass seeds tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The passage describes capability without asserting delivery.
evidence: I can export the piano's voicing records as a PDF.
That describes the workshop software's capability; I have not set a delivery date.

decisions.rationale: The author's firm delivery assertion concerns a separate ledger from the grower's hope.
evidence: I will send you our completed cooperative graft ledger tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The final explicit assurance resolves the initial plan wording.
evidence: Our plan is to send the concert piano's voicing log at noon on Friday. To be explicit, we will do so.

decisions.rationale: Delivery depends on completion of the wind survey.
evidence: We will send the course sketches when the wind survey is ready.

decisions.rationale: The passage describes completed work and past delivery.
evidence: I repaired the split hem yesterday and handed the revised condition card to the registrar.

decisions.rationale: The author directly commits to future delivery of the music-tape inventory.
evidence: I will deliver the music-tape inventory this Friday.

decisions.rationale: The prior assurance is withdrawn and replaced with a hope.
evidence: Please disregard that assurance; we now hope to send them later in the week.

decisions.rationale: Delivery is explicitly conditional on the survey being ready.
evidence: If the wind survey is ready tonight, I will get you the course sketches before tomorrow's launch.

decisions.rationale: The author directly assures delivery of the final plate.
evidence: I will send you the final cartographic plate tomorrow morning.

decisions.rationale: The withdrawal concerns granite; the separate limestone delivery is firmly asserted.
evidence: I will send you the limestone sample catalogue tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The author assures future receipt from their team.
evidence: You will receive the matching accession envelopes from our curation team by noon tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The author explicitly negates delivery and retracts the earlier assurance.
evidence: I will not deliver the restoration cue sheets tomorrow; that earlier assurance was a mistake.

decisions.rationale: Delivery occurred in the past.
evidence: I delivered the community radio tape inventory last Tuesday.

decisions.rationale: The promise is quoted from the donor rather than newly asserted by the author.
evidence: The donor wrote, "I will send the accession envelopes on Thursday."

decisions.rationale: The author assures receipt before an event, which supplies a deadline.
evidence: Before the first kite launches, you will have the printed course sketches from our organising team.

decisions.rationale: The dispatch is already completed.
evidence: Yesterday I dispatched the accession packets for all twelve meadow collections.

decisions.rationale: The author unconditionally assures receipt by a specified deadline.
evidence: You will receive the completed tapestry condition cards from me by Thursday afternoon.

decisions.rationale: The opening briefing supplies a deadline for an unconditional delivery assertion.
evidence: I will deliver the regatta course sketches before the opening briefing.

decisions.rationale: Both catalogue deliveries depend on approval.
evidence: If the quarry manager approves the sample list, I will send both catalogues on Friday. Without that approval, neither will be sent.

decisions.rationale: The phrase 'can promise' explicitly assures delivery.
evidence: Still, I can promise that I will deliver the voicing records tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The author asserts scheduled future-progressive delivery for the tested bell.
evidence: For the tested bell, our team will be handing over the signed acoustic certificate at 10 tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The promise belongs to the quoted grower and her nursery staff.
evidence: Mara, the grower, told me, "We will send the graft ledger on Monday." Her 'we' refers to the nursery staff.

decisions.rationale: A new firm commitment explicitly covers reel one's cue sheet.
evidence: I will send the completed cue sheet for reel one on Friday.

decisions.rationale: Delivery depends on uncertain cooling sufficient for testing.
evidence: If the bronze has cooled enough for the resonance test, we will deliver the acoustic certificate on Tuesday.

decisions.rationale: The author asks the recipient to send the plates.
evidence: Could you send me the annotated cave-survey plates before the archive meeting?

decisions.rationale: The author directly asserts scheduled future-progressive delivery.
evidence: At 9 tomorrow morning, we will be handing over the updated tape inventory to the station librarian.

decisions.rationale: The author requests completion and return of the cards by the recipient.
evidence: Please enter the display-case numbers on the textile condition cards and return them to me.

decisions.rationale: The author commits their team to delivering its concrete ledger.
evidence: My coordination team owns the consolidated graft ledger. We will deliver it to you on Monday.

decisions.rationale: The team delivery is firmly asserted and distinguished from a separate forecast.
evidence: Our archive team will deliver the western-passage map plates to you at Friday's briefing

decisions.rationale: An intention alone does not assure delivery.
evidence: I intend to send you the voicing records on Wednesday.

decisions.rationale: The final sentence leaves unresolved whether the condition covers only granite or also the initially firm limestone delivery.
evidence: Friday's handover: I will send the limestone catalogue; the granite catalogue will follow if the sample review passes. That condition applies to the catalogue delivery.

decisions.rationale: The author records the cartographer's forecast without adopting it as an assurance.
evidence: The expedition cartographer expects her team to deliver the eastern-chamber plates next week. That is her forecast, copied into my archive notes.

decisions.rationale: Delivery depends on the casting becoming cool enough for testing.
evidence: I will send its acoustic certificate when the casting is cool enough to test.

decisions.rationale: The author explicitly promises receipt; the retraction concerns a different item.
evidence: I can promise that you will receive the corrected cue sheets tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The author merely copies the grower's delivery assertion.
evidence: She says she will deliver it on Thursday. I have only copied that statement into the cooperative's notes.

decisions.rationale: The author unconditionally commits to handing over a specific certificate.
evidence: At Monday's inspection, I will hand you the acoustic certificate for bell B17.

decisions.rationale: Receipt of sandstone is assured; the withdrawn promise concerns slate.
evidence: You will receive the sandstone sample catalogue from our estimating team by noon Monday.
